messages:
maria: Heads-up — after the node pool driver upgrade to NVIDIA 535.54 yesterday we see ~20% lower tokens/sec for long sequences (>512). Canary numbers from dedicated-prod-PoolB.
kevin: Confirmed on my repro: seq=1024 perf drops and kernel selection reverted to the generic unfused attention path. Logs: `KERNEL_PICK: attn_unfused` where we used to pick `attn_fused_ampere_512`.
alex: Can you paste a perf trace/snippet? curious if it's an algo fallback from cuBLAS or a kernel compile issue.
maria: Perf sample attached inline — reduced to the important bits: 
```
[profile] model: llama-13b
seq_len: 1024
chosen_kernel: attn_unfused
avg_token_ms: 18.4 (was 14.6)
kv_memcpy: +30% at first decode step
cuBLAS reported algos: algo=0x3f fallback
```
kevin: That cuBLAS algo id change smells like driver math library behavior. 535 apparently changed heuristics for certain matmul sizes, which causes our autotuner to consider those algos slower and pick the conservative path.
olivia: Also noticed clobbered KV placement for certain batch/seq combos — memcpy spike at seq borders. Might be related to our buffer alignment assumptions with the new driver.
samir: Short-term mitigation: we can add a runtime override to prefer the fused-attn kernel for Ampere+ when seq>512. That avoids depending on cuBLAS algo picks. I can draft a PR.
tiago: Ops note — rolling back system driver across all Prod nodes is risky. Prefer application-level fallback if possible. But we should have a rollback playbook if perf doesn't stabilize.
alex: Agreed. Plan proposal: (1) Push runtime kernel-selection override as a hotfix and canary to 5% traffic. (2) Monitor p50/p95 token latency and per-token cost. (3) If no improvement, then escalate to driver rollback on a small pool.
maria: I created a perf-issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/2345 with traces and a reproducer. Assigned to @samir.
samir: Draft PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/897 — adds KERNEL_SELECTOR env var which can force kernel families by arch+seq range. Example config: `KERNEL_SELECTOR=ampere:>512:prefer=attn_fused_ampere`
kevin: Nice. Can we make the selector apply only to model routes with traffic > X or only to Dedicated/Dedicated-canary? We don't want to change hosted customers without opt-in.
samir: Yes — it's a node config flag for Dedicated pools; hosted remains unchanged unless we flip feature flag at control plane. I'll add route-level gating.
deploybot: deploy started: runtime-hotfix-samir PR-897 -> canary pool (dedicated-pool-b-canary) at 2026-03-17T14:12:30Z :rocket:
maria: Canary metrics after 10m: p50 token latency down 12% vs previous canary baseline, p95 down 9%, throughput back to within 3% of pre-upgrade. KV memcpy reduced.
tilago: (typo) — tiago: Nice. What's the rollback plan if canary fails?
maria: Rollback plan: 1) Revert selector (instant) and route traffic back. 2) If that fails or uncovers new regressions, rollback driver only on a small node pool (pool-c) to 525.xx and run 10% traffic. 3) If driver rollback helps, schedule full driver roll back/outage over weekend with SRE.
alex: For longer-term: update autotuner to sample algorithm latencies under multiple driver versions and keep a per-driver/kernel preference table. Also fix the KV alignment issue we saw.
olivia: I'll open an eval to track quality/regressions tied to kernel switches — want to catch any output diffs.
tiago: I'll prepare the driver rollback runbook just in case: checklist, test nodes, rollback script, and stakeholder comms.
maria: Thanks all. Action items: samir -> merge hotfix and add route gating; tiago -> rollback runbook; olivia -> eval for diffs; kevin -> follow up on autotuner improvements. I'll monitor for the next hour and then expand canary if stable. :thumbsup:
